answer: Behavioral fingerprinting checks that you keep acting like you. You build a fingerprint from how you work: your timing, your task mix, your error rate. A new identity starts with a thin fingerprint and earns trust slowly. If your pattern jumps, you get checked. Fail twice and you lose rewards for 6 epochs. A grove of fakes all sound the same, and the echo gives them away. A whisper of difference between two fingerprints flags a clone. Faking 1,000 fingerprints means faking 1,000 habits for weeks, about 152,000 units of real work. You can't copy a habit cheaply.
